report.program: Lung health education, school asthma response, research and policy

what: Respiratory Health Association provides lung-health education and works on asthma, COPD, tobacco and air quality.
Its school asthma work helps staff prepare for respiratory emergencies with training, equipment and rescue medication.
Research, caregiver support and policy advocacy complement those practical services.
strengths: Prompt asthma response offers a concrete acute health mechanism.
School staff training and stocked medication can reach students before emergency escalation.
Current institutional reporting and original returns make implementation scale and costs inspectable.
reservations: Cumulative medication uses and reported avoided ER visits are not a causal annual outcome estimate.
State funding, school nurses and existing inhalers materially constrain donor additionality.
Local household resources, outside payer costs and marginal funding capacity are unknown.

sections.what: Respiratory Health Association, EIN 36-2222687, is the whole recipient for education, research, policy and events. RESCUE Illinois Schools supplies medication, equipment and training with state support; statewide eligibility intersects Chicago counties but does not prove their actual caseload. This model uses a hypothetical Chicago local branch, not all Illinois outcomes. [Current asthma programs](https://resphealth.org/asthma-programs/)
sections.monitoring: RHA reports cumulative medication use and alleged avoided ER visits, not a verified annual causal outcome for unique Chicago students. Request local student and household counts, severity, access to alternative inhalers, repeated events, emergency care and parent work/care outcomes. Current state funding requires health and economic evaluation; required reporting is not itself evidence of realized benefits.
sections.qualitative: Prepared staff and prompt rescue medication may prevent acute asthma escalation. The model uses 500 hypothetical local households, a 25% annual-package response and a separate 20% incremental acute improvement rate; these are judgments, not observed causal rates. Each avoided event receives 0.003 QALY—about 1.1 healthy days, once—not lifelong asthma recovery, mortality prevention or survivor wages. Existing state funding, school nurses and personal inhalers remain alternatives. Other lung, research and policy effects remain unpriced.
sections.cost:
The original FY2025 return records $3,564,916 in Part IX expenses, plus $368,911 of fundraising costs and $64,394 of rental costs netted separately against revenue: $3,998,221 in gross recognized costs. The comparable 2023–2025 mean is $3,923,552.33. Donated resources outside recognized accounting remain unknown. [Original FY2025 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631359349305888/IRS990)

The conditional model exposes 125 of 500 hypothetical local households to additional work. A separate 20% clinical improvement rate gives 25 acute events avoided, valued at 0.003 QALY each after one year's delay: 0.0728155 clinical QALYs. Separately, 25 households receive a judged $400 one-time net work/care resource gain. Halving positive gains for possible health overlap, then subtracting a full $20 process burden, gives $180 per changed household; the other 100 households lose $20. One welfare person per household and a $40,000 resource baseline give 0.0302112 signed resource equivalents using the logarithmic bridge.

Combined impact is 0.1030268 equivalents, implying about $388.1M per better life. These are initial planning assumptions, not measured donation returns. Whole-recipient annual cost covers more than this local acute pathway. Null, adverse, full-response, matched-payer and three-year-cost sensitivities remain inspectable. Negative changes receive no positive-overlap discount; burdens remain when clinical benefit fails. Wider portfolio effects, nonlocal payer losses and marginal donor capacity remain unknown.
sections.funding:
The FY2025 return reports $1,337,733 of government grants and $1,661,969 of net assets. The current Illinois listing names a $535,000 award for July2026–June2027 and requires health and economic evaluation. This is an existing funded baseline, not evidence of additional donor capacity. [Illinois grant listing](https://omb.illinois.gov/public/gata/csfa/Program.aspx?csfa=2343)

RHA's July2025–June2026 report describes education and advocacy, including an inhaler copay cap effective January2026. Those existing policy benefits are not assigned to this acute branch or automatically attributed to new gifts. An unrestricted gift supports the whole recipient; request an incremental work plan, local coverage and funding substitutions. [Official annual report](https://resphealth.org/about-us/annual-report/) [Giving](https://resphealth.org/support-us/)
